world.purpose: Metric-selectable maps of published PVS reference percentages, accompanied by the separately identified Thai sample estimate. Countries without a published value stay grey. Country differences are descriptive and not a harmonised ranking.

validity_repairs.method: Shapely make_valid after coordinate rounding; retain polygonal components, discard degenerate lines

world.special_spatial_scopes: See content/international/spatial-scope.json: Argentina stays grey; Mendoza-only data use a point at the provincial capital. Thailand is a distinct reference for the unweighted sample in 13 selected provinces, not a nationwide estimate. TOTAL is not mapped.
world.international_data: content/international/values.csv; per-metric source/recall definitions in metrics.json and sources.json

processing: Kept only public geometry, public administrative names and label coordinates. Thailand: Douglas–Peucker simplification using Shapely preserve_topology=True, tolerance 0.006 degrees, followed by 4-decimal coordinate rounding; neighbouring geometries were simplified independently, so these are illustrative map boundaries, not analytical polygons. World: no added geometric simplification, only 4-decimal coordinate rounding and property trimming. Thailand label points are geometry-derived representative interior points; world labels are Natural Earth LABEL_X/LABEL_Y. No respondent locations used. After world coordinate rounding, two invalid geometries (SDN self-intersection and PRK degenerate ring) were repaired with Shapely make_valid, retaining polygon components only; repair intersections can have more than four decimal places.

international_reference.comparison_limit: Foreign PVS surveys and the unweighted Thai achieved sample differ in frames, weighting, dates, mode and interpretation. Unmet need refers to the past 12 months in both Thailand and foreign PVS; Thai original questionnaire confirmed by the researcher on 2026-10-01; Argentina means Mendoza Province only. No country ranking or causal inference.
